vagrantfile.scenario: A single-machine Vagrantfile has a material DSL question
vagrantfile.expected: Trigger the profile and establish Vagrant and configuration version, host, provider, file ownership, and project policy

vagrantfile.scenario: An ordinary Ruby task has no Vagrant behavior
vagrantfile.expected: Non-trigger; use the Ruby or project owner when independently material

vagrantfile.scenario: A task changes only Terraform or Docker behavior
vagrantfile.expected: Non-trigger; route to the applicable infrastructure or project owner

vagrantfile.scenario: The configuration version is unsupported or unknown
vagrantfile.expected: Red until the supported configuration API and selected Vagrant behavior are established

vagrantfile.scenario: Configuration is loaded conditionally from uncontrolled host state
vagrantfile.expected: Orange while bounding branches and inputs; protected, unbounded, or falsely portable behavior is Red

vagrantfile.scenario: Plugin behavior is assumed without version evidence
vagrantfile.expected: Orange until exact plugin and Vagrant compatibility are established; a consequential support claim without evidence is Red

vagrantfile.scenario: A box version floats
vagrantfile.expected: Yellow or Orange under project update policy; a consequential immutable or supported claim without evidence is Red

vagrantfile.scenario: A project-approved exact box version has checksum or metadata evidence
vagrantfile.expected: Green or Yellow after source, provider, architecture, update, provenance, and rollback boundaries are verified; do not infer boot success

vagrantfile.scenario: A private box URL or credential is involved
vagrantfile.expected: Red if protected data can enter source, environment, URL, logs, state, or artifacts; use only a project-approved protected transport

vagrantfile.scenario: A provider-specific block targets an approved provider
vagrantfile.expected: Green or Yellow after exact provider version, availability, override, capability, host, and rollback boundaries are established

vagrantfile.scenario: Provider-specific behavior is assumed to be portable
vagrantfile.expected: Red until each claimed provider and host variant is established

vagrantfile.scenario: A required plugin is missing
vagrantfile.expected: Red until the exact name, version requirement, source, and compatibility are resolved; do not install it

vagrantfile.scenario: Plugin installation is requested without authority
vagrantfile.expected: Red authority and global-state stop

vagrantfile.scenario: One simple machine has bounded configuration
vagrantfile.expected: Green when its effective box, provider, network, folder, provisioner, state, and policy boundaries are explicit

vagrantfile.scenario: A coherent multi-machine environment shares one topology and lifecycle
vagrantfile.expected: Green or Yellow while concrete fan-out, dependencies, command breadth, and rollback remain bounded

vagrantfile.scenario: Dynamic machine generation obscures ownership
vagrantfile.expected: Orange until every concrete machine and attached declaration is bounded; representing an unbounded result as verified is Red

vagrantfile.scenario: Forwarded ports can collide
vagrantfile.expected: Red until exact machine, host address, host and guest port, protocol, allocation, consumer, and rollback are collision-free

vagrantfile.scenario: A forwarded port is privileged or publicly exposed
vagrantfile.expected: Red until explicit exposure and privilege authority, host binding, firewall, validation, and rollback are accepted

vagrantfile.scenario: A private-network static address conflicts
vagrantfile.expected: Red until address ownership, subnet, provider, host routes, peer allocation, and rollback are reconciled

vagrantfile.scenario: A public network exposes a guest
vagrantfile.expected: Red until exact intended exposure, provider meaning, host interface, guest hardening, firewall, validation, and rollback are accepted

vagrantfile.scenario: Host-only network assumptions differ by provider or platform
vagrantfile.expected: Orange pending exact provider, host, address, route, and capability evidence; a portable claim is Red

vagrantfile.scenario: A narrow project-owned host folder is synced to an exact guest path
vagrantfile.expected: Green or Yellow after effective layers, type, provider, ownership, permissions, symlinks, direction, and rollback are established

vagrantfile.scenario: A host home directory or broad sensitive path is mounted
vagrantfile.expected: Red host-data exposure stop

vagrantfile.scenario: Synced-folder ownership, permissions, or symlink behavior is unclear
vagrantfile.expected: Orange until the host, guest, provider, type, ownership, mode, and link contract is explicit; unsafe exposure is Red

vagrantfile.scenario: A provider-specific synced-folder implementation is selected
vagrantfile.expected: Green or Yellow only under approved provider and plugin policy with exact version, capability, path, and rollback evidence

vagrantfile.scenario: Project policy disables the default folder
vagrantfile.expected: Green or Yellow after confirming the effective layered configuration, dependent guest paths, provisioning assumptions, and rollback

vagrantfile.scenario: A project-approved provisioner is designed to be idempotent
vagrantfile.expected: Green or Yellow after repeat, failure, privilege, input, output, validation, and rollback evidence; the declaration alone is not proof

vagrantfile.scenario: A shell provisioner uses a fixed argument vector
vagrantfile.expected: Yellow after guest OS, transport, interpreter, privilege, quoting, environment, repeatability, and rollback are established; pair a shell profile only when independently material

vagrantfile.scenario: An untrusted value reaches shell interpretation
vagrantfile.expected: Red source-to-shell stop

vagrantfile.scenario: A non-idempotent provisioner can repeat destructive effects
vagrantfile.expected: Red until authority, repetition control, adverse-case validation, and rollback are established

vagrantfile.scenario: A destroy or halt trigger mutates external state
vagrantfile.expected: Red without exact lifecycle authority; an authorized design remains Orange until ordering, failure, idempotency, validation, and rollback are accepted

vagrantfile.scenario: Trigger ordering or failure behavior is unclear
vagrantfile.expected: Orange until scope, order, host or guest execution, failure mode, and partial-effect recovery are explicit; destructive ambiguity is Red

vagrantfile.scenario: Secrets appear in inline provisioning or logs
vagrantfile.expected: Red protected-data stop

vagrantfile.scenario: .vagrant state is treated as source
vagrantfile.expected: Red truthfulness and state-ownership stop; classify it as generated machine/provider identity

vagrantfile.scenario: Machine identity or provider state is stale or shared incorrectly
vagrantfile.expected: Red until source, local state, global index, provider identity, ownership, backup, and recovery are reconciled without manual mutation

vagrantfile.scenario: A task requests vagrant up, reload, provision, or destroy without authority
vagrantfile.expected: Red lifecycle-authority stop

vagrantfile.scenario: A Vagrantfile branches on host platform
vagrantfile.expected: Yellow or Orange while exact branches, supported hosts, provider capabilities, inputs, and tests are bounded; uncontrolled or falsely portable behavior is Red

vagrantfile.scenario: The Vagrantfile is generated or vendor-owned
vagrantfile.expected: Classify and change the authorized generator or owner; semantic Red stops still control

vagrantfile.scenario: Repository policy is stricter than the profile fallback
vagrantfile.expected: Stricter repository policy controls

vagrantfile.scenario: Vagrantfile structure crosses a warning or crisis threshold
vagrantfile.expected: Apply classification, concrete expansion, coupling, decomposition, bounded-exception, and rollback rules
